title: WPMS/2667/2019 of M/S DABUR INDIA LIMITED Vs DEEPAK KUMAR JOSHI

paras.text:
WPMS No. 2667 of 2019
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Heard Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate, assisted by
Mr. Aditya Kumar Arya, Advocate for the petitioner.
This is employer's writ petition against the orders
dated 21.02.2019 and 01.08.2019 passed by Presiding
Officer, Labour Court Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar
in Adjudication Case No. 30 of 2011.
Pursuant to an industrial dispute raised by the
respondent, following reference was referred to the Labour
Court Kashipur for adjudication:-
"Whether termination of services of workman
Mr. Deepak Kumar Joshi, S/o Shrish Chandra Joshi,
R/o Village and Post Haripura, Tehsild Bazpur,
District Udham Singh Nagar by the employer w.e.f.
06.03.2010 is legal or justified? If not, then what relief
the workman is entitled to alongwith which
particulars."
 After exchange of pleadings, the workman
(respondent herein) moved an application before the Labour
Court to summon Mr. Govind Reddy, Unit Head of the
petitioner as witness, besides the officials in the Office of
Assistant Labour Commissioner and Deputy Labour
Commissioner.
Learned Labour Court allowed the said application
vide order dated 21.02.2019. Thus, feeling aggrieved, the
employer has approached this Court against summoning of
its Unit Head as witness and he is not aggrieved by that part
of the order, whereby officials of Labour Department have
been summoned.
A plaintiff cannot normally compel the defendant to
appear before the Court as a witness. The practice of citing
the opposite party as a witness has been condemned as an
unapproved form of evidence. If such a practice is allowed,
it would result in cross-examination by his own counsel.
To illustrate, if the Unit Head of the petitioner is examined
by the respondent's counsel, the counsel of petitioner gets
the opportunity to cross-examine his own client. This is an
unwholesome practice.
Such a practice was condemned by the Privy
Counsel in Kishori Lal v. Chunni Lal reported in 1908
SCC OnLine P.C. 21, where it was held:

"As to this last matter, it would appear from
the judgment of the High Court that in India it
is one of the artifices of a weak and somewhat
paltry kind of advocacy for each litigant to
cause his opponent to be summoned as a
witness, with the design that each party shall
be forced to produce the opponent so
summoned as witness, and thus give the
counsel for each litigant the opportunity of
cross-examining his own client. It is a practice
which their Lordships cannot help thinking all
judicial tribunals ought to set themselves to
render as abortive as it is objectionable. It
ought never to be permitted in the result to
embarrass judicial investigation as it has done
in this instance."
In Koshy Eapen v. Idikula Varghese (V T.L.T. 271) a
Division Bench of the High Court of Travancore held that the
practice of citing the opposite party as a witness, has to be
condemned as an unapproved form of evidence.
Similar view was taken by Kerala High Court
in Narayana Pillay v. Kallyani Amma (1963 KLT 537).
It is true that the Court is not powerless in summoning
the opposite party if there are special reasons. No such
reasons have been made out in the instant case to compel
Unit Head of the petitioner to give evidence for and on behalf
of the respondent.
In such view of the matter, the writ petition is allowed
and the impugned order dated 21.02.2019 is set-aside only to
the extent of summoning of Unit Head of the petitioner.
Other part of the order dated 21.02.2019 shall remain intact.
Consequently, the order dated 01.08.2019, whereby bailable
warrant was issued against Mr. Govind Reddy is also set-aside.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the
Unit Head, Mr. Govind Reddy, will soon enter the witness
box after close of workman evidence to prove the case of the
employer. Thus, the respondent shall have the opportunity to
cross-examine him.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Navin 05.09.2019
